evidence.claim: Anthropic's inference revenue per megawatt went from about $16M to over $60M in a year across its fleet; June-quarter revenue up 1,368% against compute expense up 300%. The value per megawatt of a site is set by the model and software on it, not the hall: the lab earns about 30x the landlord's rent on the same megawatt.
evidence.numbers: $16M to $60M+ per MW per year; revenue +1,368% vs compute cost +300%
evidence.source: SemiAnalysis on Anthropic's S-1, 27 Oct 2026 (not yet checked against the filing)

evidence.claim: A listed cloud provider took a 20 MW, 10-year colocation lease from Q2 2027 for more than $400M over the term.
evidence.numbers: Supports demand for sites of tens of MW from established cloud tenants.

evidence.claim: Muse, Meta's consumer agent, is 'very compute intensive'. Meta targets more than 10x cost efficiency in a year through off-peak capacity, smaller models and inference optimization, and wants to serve as much high-margin inference as possible.
evidence.numbers: Muse >10mn users in US/Canada in ~6 weeks, ~25% daily use; total serving costs expected to rise.

evidence.claim: Split its 2026 TPU into inference and training chips, projecting inference at 30–60% of demand; serving clusters run from one rack to tens of MW.
Brian Janous says the smallest site a desperate buyer will accept is about 50 MW.
Agents have created a CPU shortage, since CPUs orchestrate agent workloads.
CoreWeave's ~$21bn expansion with Meta (through Dec 2032, Vera Rubin) is framed as capacity to scale Meta's inference workloads.
evidence.numbers: ~$21bn on top of the ~$14.2bn Sept 2025 deal.

evidence.claim: Predicts about 90% of AI load will be inference within 3–4 years, with 5–30 MW city sites (vendor claim).

question: Are agents and inference changing what sites need: size, CPUs, storage, location?
summary: Inference is taking a growing share and needs different sites: smaller, spread out, with more CPUs and storage beside the accelerators. That widens the market for sites of tens of megawatts, though large tenants still prefer 50 MW or more.
title: Inference changing site design
